narrative:
The model predicts you have a 28% chance of failing your final year, which is high enough that the school requires you to take remedial courses as a precaution.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this prediction were your number of past class failures, your father's education level, and the reason you chose this school. Having no previous failures was the strongest element and pushed the prediction toward passing. However, this positive influence was outweighed by the other two features. Your father having only primary education pulled the outcome noticeably toward failure; among students who passed, far more had parents with secondary or higher education. Similarly, choosing the school because it was close to home also worked against you. Most students who passed chose the school for its course offerings or reputation rather than location.

Taken together, these elements led the model to conclude you are at risk of not passing. To improve your chances, you should focus on building strong study habits now, since your current weekly study time is under two hours while most successful students study 2–5 hours. Consider talking with your teachers about extra academic support and making fuller use of the fact that you have internet access at home for learning resources. Small, consistent improvements in daily study routines can meaningfully change your trajectory before the final exams.
